headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared-file and output-chaining pathways can create prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors; no direct evidence of stronger isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can touch documents, personal data, and workflows, while great_expectations reads files and writes validation results/documentation. A shared workspace or manual handoff could let attacker-controlled file content from A influence B’s parsing. No direct shared-channel evidence is present, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into a shared directory that agent_b reads
IF agent_b parses document text from agent_a as instructions
mitigations: Separate input/output folders per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of agent_a-generated documents
Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes agent_a outputs
Use file provenance labels in filenames
requires-engineering: enforce sandboxed mounts per agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a explicitly touches personal data and finance data, and agent_b reads/writes files including validation results and documentation. If those files contain sensitive records, the pair can move data across the shared workspace. Because no explicit isolation or redaction is documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF sensitive records are stored in files that agent_b validates
IF agent_a-generated documents include personal or finance data
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to synthetic or masked datasets
Store sensitive inputs in a separate directory with access controls
Review validation outputs before sharing them outside the workspace
Delete temporary exports after each run
requires-engineering: add automated redaction before file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has allowlisted network egress and session-scoped concurrency, while agent_b can install packages but has no network egress. Their write surfaces do not clearly overlap in the profiles, so a direct resource conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because shared filesystem or git state is not described.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF package installation by agent_b modifies files that agent_a also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pin package installs to an isolated environment
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project tree
Use a lock file for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and great_expectations produces validation results and documentation. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative inputs, an error in A can propagate into B’s reports or checks. No verification chain is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows and merits medium.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated decisions or workflows as test inputs
IF agent_b renders agent_a outputs without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review of agent_a outputs before B consumes them
Add schema checks on all handoff files
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default
Compare B results against a baseline dataset
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b handles files for validation results and documentation. If the same regulated data class is routed through both, retention or residency mismatches could create a compliance gap. The profiles do not document certifications or residency, so uncertainty again favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is written into agent_b-managed files
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b outputs
Document retention rules for both agents
Use anonymized datasets for validation
Review logs for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
